entries.test: Whether frontier capability gains from late 2024 to early 2025 came mainly from techniques beyond pure LLM pretraining scale-up, such as test-time compute or reasoning training, rather than from simply adding data and compute.
entries.note: The 'bears out' part is Marcus grading his own essay. The part that can be checked is whether new techniques were needed.

entries.test: Whether, once pure LLM scaling showed diminishing returns, several labs reached similar frontier performance and competed heavily on price, with no lasting moat for any lab.
entries.note: Readers may disagree on whether the antecedent (pure scaling running out) has happened. 'You would expect' is a firm expectation, not probability language.

entries.test: Whether by early 2025 several labs (e.g. DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) had similar top-model performance and were cutting API prices against each other, as OpenAI did after DeepSeek R1.
entries.note: 'Diminishing returns' is the vaguest part. The price war and crowding at the top are easier to check.
Readers would score an essay as right 'in most other respects' in different ways. The specific sub-claims are better graded on their own.
This combines a value judgment ('deeply misplaced') with a polemical description of 'oligarchs'.
